evidence.detail: Launcher checks this class's static editor-mode flag and changes the client window title to the literal 'SPK Editor Kit' while also switching the normal launcher/UI layout for that mode.

The live loading controller constructs exactly one rs/l/b/a/d(Client), stores it in the class singleton, and immediately initializes it when Editor Kit mode is active; Client loop/input/camera paths later call back into that same singleton.
The class owns the live Editor Kit command surface for npc, player, item, delete/del, reset/wipe, reverse, hud, background/bg plus per-entity movement and animation commands.

It owns the editor entity list, active graphics context, camera position/curve/zoom state, background color, HUD/mode flags and status-message output. Surviving diagnostics include 'Camera position reset', 'Entities cleared!', 'Entity indices reversed!' and 'Graphics and definitions have been reset!'.

candidates.note: EditorKitController is descriptive exact-behavior recovery anchored by the surviving product label 'SPK Editor Kit', singleton lifecycle and command/render ownership. No surviving original class noun was found.

evidence.detail: The class is abstract and has exactly three concrete subclasses in exact v308: rs/l/b/a/a/b, rs/l/b/a/a/c and rs/l/b/a/a/d.
It owns the common Editor Kit entity position, animation definition/frame state, selection/hover state, render-order/index state and per-entity interaction collections.
Its common update method lazily initializes subclass rendering, calls the subclass render hook every tick, and advances the assigned SequenceDefinition frame cycle when an animation is active.
The shared class reads the EditorKitController singleton/Client for projection and mouse-space data, proving it is the common entity abstraction owned by that editor subsystem.

candidates.note: EditorEntity is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the shared abstract base of the three Editor Kit entity kinds.

evidence.detail: EditorKitController's live 'item' command parses one item ID, resolves ItemDefinition for the confirmation text, removes any prior item entity and constructs new rs/l/b/a/a/b(itemId).
The subclass stores only its item-specific integer beyond the EditorEntity base and exposes direct get/set access to that value.
Its render hook calls ItemDefinition sprite generation for the stored item ID and draws that item sprite in the Editor Kit overlay, alongside the editor entity selection/index visualization.
It is one of exactly three concrete subclasses of EditorEntity, alongside the independently NPC- and Player-backed subclasses.

candidates.note: EditorItemEntity is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the Editor Kit entity created by the item command and rendered from ItemDefinition sprites.

evidence.detail: The integer constructor resolves rs/d/d.c(id), the R28 NpcDefinition lookup, and the model/render path obtains the NPC definition model.
EditorKitController's live 'npc' command constructs this subclass with the requested NPC ID, assigns editor index/position and inserts it into the editor entity list.
The subclass preserves exact interaction messages 'Selected @gre@NPC entity #' and 'Deleted @red@NPC entity #'.
It is one of exactly three concrete EditorEntity subclasses and is the only one backed by NpcDefinition.

candidates.note: EditorNpcEntity is strongly fixed by direct NpcDefinition ownership, the live npc command and surviving NPC entity labels.

evidence.detail: The subclass constructs and maintains an rs/a/k Player instance and obtains its model through the Player model path while owning editor appearance/equipment state.
EditorKitController's live 'player' command constructs this subclass, assigns editor index/position and inserts it into the shared entity list.
The adjacent live player-command helper mutates this entity's appearance/equipment using named slots such as amulet, boots, cape, gloves, helmet, legs, shield and weapon plus male/female transforms.
The subclass preserves exact interaction messages 'Selected @gre@Player entity #' and 'Deleted @red@Player entity #'.

candidates.note: EditorPlayerEntity is strongly fixed by its Player-backed model path, live player command, appearance/equipment mutations and surviving Player entity labels.
